I'm really excited for BO3. I used to love Call of Duty games back in the day, but the last few entries have been severely lacking for me. I've played the beta on PS4 and PC and I was very impressed. There's nothing more satisfying than wall running, jumping, then 360 NO SCOPE Y-Y FAKE OUT GRENADE CANCEL 420XXXSWAG SHOT 9000

The weird thing for me is that the fast-paced, jumping like rabbits gameplay never appealed to me. Ghosts got a lot of flack but it's the one Call of Duty outside of Modern Warfare where I feel I could actually sneak and ambush in, where running around blindly gets you killed more often than not. I feel like Advanced Warfare was a huge move away from that, and it sounds like Black Ops is going to continue the style of Advanced Warfare in that regard. I'll get it for the co-op campaign, but I don't think I'll get into the multiplayer. I just miss the days where I could count on every other CoD being slower paced to balance out the twitch gameplay of the other games in the series.

See, I like the fast paced gameplay. There was nothing more frustrating than running around, rushing spawns, going on crazy high streaks just to get killed by someone sitting across the map laying prone with a sniper rifle, next to his claymore and bag of Cool Ranch Doritos. I get that there will always be people who play and enjoy the game like that, but it certainly doesn't appeal to me.

And really there's nothing wrong with enjoying that style of gameplay either. I'm just disappointed because it used to be that every other Call of Duty was slower paced. The Black Ops series (Treyarch) was faster paced and while I wouldn't do as well I could still play them. The Modern Warfare/Ghosts series (Infinity Ward) were the slower paced games that I excel at and enjoy very much. They used to trade off every year, so every other year I'd get a CoD I really enjoy and every other year I'd get one that I wasn't nearly as good at but still enjoyed.

Now they've added a third dev team into the mix (Sledgehammer) who did Advanced Warfare, and that game is even more twitch-focused than any of the Black Ops games. I figured I was out of luck until Infinity Ward is back up, but at least Black Ops will be easier because it's mellow compared to Advanced Warfare. But it looks like Black Ops is shaping up to follow the Advanced Warfare formula. With previous Black Ops games, stealth was more difficult but still an option, but with Advanced Warfare it isn't feasible. If BO3 follows Advanced Warfare's formula, I'll have to sit out on this one and only play every third release (Infinity Ward - unless they adopt the same style as the others). The prospects don't look good for my style of CoD game.

You didn't consider MW2* to be really fast paced? I couldn't find a game without commando knife-only, people exclusively quickscoping, using grenade launchers as long ranged shotguns, or using actual long ranged shotguns.

No, not at all. In fact, that was one of my favorites for sneaking around with a single-shot assault rifle to pick people off at range or kill someone at close range who wasn't paying enough attention to their surrounding as they run by. See, you could still run and play fast in any CoD game, but at least Modern Warfare/Ghosts would punish you for it if someone was sneaky enough to trap you. Even walking around would give you an advantage because you can bring your sights up much faster than someone breaking out of a sprint. With the recent games that doesn't matter because you still can't sight up as fast from a sprint but now you can dodge and jet pack away until you have your shot. It's like trying to shoot at a rabbit with how quickly people jump around.

The level design of Infinity Ward games is also different. Hallways and lanes branch out more, so you're more covered instead of taking fire from all sides. Black Ops/Advanced Warfare maps tend to funnel you towards the enemy and most of the fighting takes place in two opposite directions instead of branching out. In MW2 there's less of that "tunnel effect". MW3 and Ghosts are the same way. Black Ops 1 & 2 are harder, but still not as bad as Advanced Warfare.
I guess you got a point there. Guess I was just focusing on my style of gameplay, since it was never really held back in a CoD game that much.
